title: Trades by Officials, Family & Associates
summary: Disclosure filings document many well-timed trades around tariff and policy news: Attorney General Bondi's $1M-$5M+ Trump Media sale on 2 April 2025, Scavino's $1M-$5M Trump Media sale on 1 April, Duffy's February 2025 sales before the reciprocal-tariff plan, 327 purchases in one of Trump's own accounts on 8 April 2025, the day before the tariff pause (verified in his OGE annual report; disclosed on 30 June 2026, about 13 months after the 45-day deadline, with late fees paid), at least $82M of bonds bought by Trump in autumn 2025, and heavy trading by members of Congress such as Greene and Moskowitz around the 9 April pause. Pre-announcement run-ups are documented for Dominari and Unusual Machines and reported for ALT5 Sigma, but no buyer has been identified. In prediction markets the only charged US case tied to a government action is a soldier's Maduro bets. Don Jr. advises Kalshi and Polymarket and 1789 Capital invested in Polymarket, but no family bets are documented. None of the trades has led to a finding that anyone used non-public information. Officials say outside managers made the trades or that the sales were required by ethics agreements; the White House says Trump's assets are in fully discretionary accounts run by independent third-party institutions.

sub_claims.statement: Attorney General Pam Bondi sold Trump Media shares and warrants on 2 April 2025, the day of the 'Liberation Day' tariff announcement.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (her OGE periodic transaction report, made public in mid-May 2025, as reported by Bloomberg Law, CBS and ProPublica; ProPublica's report was read in full, the form itself was not). (1) Filing: a sale of Trump Media & Technology Group shares valued at $1M-$5M plus warrants valued at $250K-$500K, both dated 2 April 2025 (combined $1.25M-$5.5M by our arithmetic; Bloomberg Law gives $1M-$5.5M). ProPublica: DJT closed at $18.76 on 2 April and opened at $17.92 the next morning. The form does not give the time of day; Trump announced the tariffs after the market close that day, and DJT shares fell in the following sessions (CBS reports about 13% within days). (2) Inference by outlets: the timing was unusually fortunate. (3) Allegation: Rep. Jamie Raskin asked DOJ Inspector General Michael Horowitz on 20 May 2025 to investigate whether Bondi or other DOJ officials traded on non-public information. (4) No finding: no inspector-general result or other official finding was found as of Nov 2026. Context: her ethics agreement required her to divest the TMTG holding within 90 days of taking office (she was confirmed in early Feb 2025), so a sale in that window was required; only its date is in question. Response: the DOJ did not answer early press questions; at a June 2025 House hearing Bondi said she had complied with ethics rules and had lost money on the stock (as summarised by Ground News; the hearing record was not read). Builds on C65, which already records this sale.

sub_claims.statement: Deputy Chief of Staff Dan Scavino and personnel director Sergio Gor sold Trump Media stock days before 2 April 2025.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: Gor documented (his own OGE 278-T, signed 20 May 2025, read in full: a sale of Trump Media & Technology Group valued at $15,001-$50,000 dated 27 March 2025); Scavino single-source (USA Today, from OGE disclosures, seen through syndicated copies and Business Insider's relay; his form was not read). (1) As reported: Scavino sold Trump Media stock valued at $1M-$5M on 1 April 2025, the day before the tariff announcement, after holding it for months in office. A later report (The Washington Sun, relayed by a blog in Oct 2026) says Scavino's 2025 annual disclosure shows $1M-$5M of capital gains from the holding; that is unverified (single report via a blog, form not read). (2)/(3) USA Today said it found no evidence that either man knew of the announcement in advance; watchdogs called the timing 'striking'. (4) No inquiry or finding was found. Response: a White House spokesperson (named in reposts as assistant press secretary Taylor Rogers) said senior staff including Scavino and Gor fully comply with executive-branch ethics rules, and the White House said Gor's sale 'had nothing to do with the tariff announcement' (both via syndicated excerpts; treat the wording as unconfirmed). Scavino and Gor had not been named in earlier checks as sellers.

sub_claims.statement: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy sold stocks shortly before a tariff announcement.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (OGE records reported by ProPublica, republished by other outlets; the forms were not read). (1) Filing: Duffy sold shares in about three dozen companies (34 stocks) on 11 and 13 February 2025, together $90K-$650K in reported ranges, before and on the day Trump announced his plan for 'reciprocal' tariffs (13 February 2025). The claim as often repeated places these sales in April 2025; they were in February. (2) ProPublica said it was unclear whether Duffy had any advance information about the timing or scale of the tariff plan. (3) No official has alleged a violation on the record that we found. (4) No inquiry or finding. Response: a Transportation Department spokesperson said an outside manager made the trades in a retirement account, that Duffy 'had no input on the timing of the sales', and that his ethics agreement required him to sell seven of those holdings within his first three months. Audit: ProPublica's article (19 May 2025) was read in full and confirms 34 stocks worth $90,000-$650,000 sold on 11 and 13 February, seven of them required by the ethics agreement (the other 27 worth $27,000-$405,000), and the department's statement that the trades were made by an outside manager in a retirement account and that Duffy 'had no input on the timing of the sales'.

sub_claims.statement: More than a dozen other executive-branch officials and aides made well-timed sales before tariff announcements.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (ProPublica review of hundreds of disclosures, 22 May 2025, read in full). (1) Named in excerpts: Gautam Rana, a longtime State Department official who was ambassador to Slovakia when ProPublica reported, sold $830K-$1.7M of stock, largely broad index funds, on 19 March 2025, a week before the car tariffs and two weeks before 2 April; a career lawyer serving as acting general counsel of the White House Office of Administration (named by ProPublica) sold an index fund and nine companies ($12K-$180K) the day before Trump confirmed the Mexico and Canada tariffs; a trade-office (USTR) official sold $2K-$30K of Target and Freeport-McMoRan on 25 and 27 March. (2) ProPublica itself states there is no evidence that any of the trades it identified were informed by non-public information. (3) No authority has alleged wrongdoing that we found. (4) No finding. Responses: officials either said they had no inside information or did not respond; State Department official Stephanie Syptak-Ramnath said she had no information beyond what was public and traded because of family obligations and a changing economy; Rana declined to comment; the Office of Administration lawyer said his wife made the sale from her own account to pay tuition and that he had no nonpublic information; the USTR official did not respond.

sub_claims.statement: Trump's own accounts bought stocks the day before the 9 April 2025 tariff pause, and the trades were disclosed late.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (Trump's OGE Form 278e annual report for 2025, received by OGE on 29 June 2026 and made public on 30 June; the cover page and Part 7 were read in full from the PDF). (1) Filing: our count of Part 7 finds 327 transactions dated 8 April 2025, all purchases, all in the account labelled 'Investment Account #7'. By range: 139 at $1,001-$15,000, 176 at $15,001-$50,000, 7 at $50,001-$100,000 and 5 at $100,001-$250,000, which sums to $3.63M-$12.84M. Names include Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Amazon and Alphabet. No transactions are listed on 7 or 9 April. The same account made 462 transactions (224 purchases, 238 sales) on 4 April and 273 purchases ($3.0M-$10.5M) on 10 April, and the report lists about 21,000 transactions across eight accounts in 2025, so 8 April was one of many heavy-trading days; ABC News noted that the account made similar trades through the year and traded more in volatile periods, consistent with rebalancing. Late disclosure: the reviewing official's comments (dated 30 June 2026) read 'The filer was granted a 45-day extension to file this annual report' and 'The filer paid late filing fees related to transactions not previously reported on 278-Ts.' The note does not say which transactions or how much was paid; Sludge reports that no 278-T covered the April trades or virtually any 2025 stock trade, and that the statutory late fee is $200. A 278-T is due within 30 days of notification and no later than 45 days after a trade, so these trades surfaced about 13 months after the deadline and nearly 15 months after they were made. On 9 April the S&P 500 rose about 9.5%. (2) Outlets infer the timing is notable; the filing does not show who placed or directed the trades, the time of day, or any gain. (3) Critics and Democratic members (including Sen. Schiff and Rep. Levin) have cited the trades and asked for full disclosure; no authority has alleged a violation that we found. (4) No finding. Responses: the White House has said all of the President's assets are held in 'fully discretionary accounts managed by independent third-party financial institutions' and that there are no conflicts of interest (wording attributed to spokesperson Anna Kelly; repeated in July 2026 coverage, though the original occasion was not confirmed); ABC News reported that the White House said the accounts are run by professional advisers who do not regularly communicate with Trump, and Trump told reporters 'I'm profiting? Because the stock market's going up, everybody's profiting'; a spokesperson also pointed to trading by former Speaker Nancy Pelosi. The Trump Organization said in May 2026 (of the 2026 trades) that neither Trump, his family nor the company 'plays any role in selecting, directing, or approving specific investments' and that they 'receive no advance notice of trading activity'. The accounts are not a blind trust. This is a material addition to C58, which addressed only unidentified options traders around the pause.

sub_claims.statement: Trump bought large amounts of corporate and municipal bonds while in office, including debt of companies affected by his policies.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (OGE Form 278-T filings released in Nov 2025, reported by Reuters and Bloomberg; the forms were listed in search results but could not be opened). (1) Filings: at least $82M of corporate and municipal bonds bought between late August and early October 2025; because amounts are ranges the upper bound exceeds $337M (Reuters). Most is municipal and public-sector debt; corporate issuers include Broadcom, Qualcomm, Meta, Home Depot, CVS Health, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan Chase, and Reuters-based reports say the accounts bought Intel bonds shortly after the government took its Intel stake in August 2025. A trade-publication tally puts bond purchases for the term at over $104M (single-source). (2) Watchdogs describe these as potential conflicts because the issuers are affected by tariff, technology and financial-regulation policy. (3)/(4) No allegation of trading on non-public information by an authority and no finding. Response: a White House official said Trump does not manage his portfolio, which is overseen by a third-party institution, and that he files the required disclosures. Later 2026 filings (Q1 2026: about 3,600-3,700 trades, including Palantir, Nvidia and a 10 Feb 2026 Dell purchase months before he praised Dell) are covered in C20 and C68 and not repeated here.

sub_claims.statement: Members of Congress bought or sold stocks around the 9 April 2025 tariff pause.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (House periodic transaction reports as reported by Bloomberg, Business Insider, Fortune, CNN and the Campaign Legal Center; the PTRs were not read). (1) Filings: Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene reported purchases in about 17-20 companies (including Tesla, Amazon, Apple, Nvidia, Palantir, Blackstone) dated mainly 8-9 April 2025 (some outlets add 2 April or 3-4 April), together $21,021-$315,000, and a sale of Treasuries of $50,001-$100,000 on 8 April; she filed on 11 April. Rep. Jared Moskowitz bought $20K-$300K across about 20 companies on 7 April (Business Insider; The Bulwark gives up to $345K). Rep. Rob Bresnahan reported 171 trades on 8 April (single-source: one published data chart); Rep. Ro Khanna reported 438 transactions from 31 March to 9 April (CNN; CLC counts 446 over a different window); Rep. Kevin Hern reported the largest single transaction, up to $5M, on 4 April (CNN; direction not given in the excerpts). The Campaign Legal Center counted 53 members making over 2,200 trades worth $34.9M-$140M between 13 February and 9 April 2025, split roughly evenly by party. (2) House disclosure ranges do not show profit or loss (Fortune). (3) Critics and the NRCC (against Moskowitz) questioned the timing; CLC used the data to argue for a trading ban rather than alleging insider trading. (4) No House Ethics or other official finding on these trades was found in this research. Responses: Greene denied insider trading, said her portfolio manager 'bought the dip' and told ProPublica 'Since my portfolio manager makes my trades for me, I usually find out about them when the media asks', and called calls for an investigation 'utterly absurd'; Moskowitz's spokesperson said all his trades are 'managed by an outside third-party financial advisor' (Business Insider, read in full); Khanna's office said the transactions were in a trust managed by an independent third party; Bresnahan said he never trades 'my own stocks' and later added guardrails on his account; no response from Hern was found.

sub_claims.statement: Small listed companies saw unusual trading before Trump family involvement was announced (Dominari, Unusual Machines, PSQ, GrabAGun, American Bitcoin/Gryphon, ALT5 Sigma).
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented for price and volume moves in two cases; no trader identified in any case. Dominari: a roughly 530-580% six-week run-up before the 11 Feb 2025 announcement, with no buyer identified (C39, C91; not repeated). Unusual Machines: shares rose more than 220% in the four weeks before Don Jr. joined its advisory board on 27 Nov 2024 (before the term began), with volume well above earlier 2024 (FT); the company said knowledge of his planned involvement was limited to three senior officers, the board and counsel. PSQ Holdings: shares nearly tripled on the day (3 Dec 2024) reports said Don Jr. would join its board; no pre-announcement run-up was reported. GrabAGun: fell about 24% on its July 2025 debut; no pre-announcement anomaly reported (C39). Gryphon/American Bitcoin: spike came on the 12 May 2025 announcement, no reported run-up (C91). ALT5 Sigma: The Block reported 'some evidence of unusual trading activity' before the 11 Aug 2025 WLFI-treasury announcement while stating ALT5 is not accused of wrongdoing; price figures for the days before conflict between outlets, and the stock fell on the day (C13 did not record this). Regulators: the WSJ reported in Sept 2025 that the SEC and FINRA had contacted some of the 200+ crypto-treasury companies about volume and price spikes before announcements; outlets did not establish that ALT5 was among them, and one secondary report naming Trump Media among the companies under scrutiny is unconfirmed. No enforcement action, named trader or official finding was found for any of these companies through Nov 2026.

sub_claims.statement: Traders have been identified for prediction-market bets tied to government decisions.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented for charged cases; none involves a Trump administration political official or family member. US: Army Master Sgt. Gannon Ken Van Dyke was indicted in SDNY (unsealed 23 April 2026) on five counts (unlawful use of confidential government information, theft of nonpublic government information, commodities fraud, wire fraud and an unlawful monetary transaction), alongside a CFTC civil case; he pleaded not guilty and trial is set for 7 December 2026, for allegedly using classified information about the Maduro operation to win more than $400K on Polymarket; Polymarket says it identified and referred the trades. The case is an allegation pending trial (C58). Not a government decision but the second US case: Google employee Michele Spagnuolo ('AlphaRaccoon') was charged on 27 May 2026 over about $1.2M of Polymarket bets on Google search rankings. Abroad: Israel indicted an IDF reservist and a civilian in Feb 2026 for allegedly using classified information about Israeli military operations to bet on Polymarket (reported winnings about $150K-$162K). Kalshi fined and suspended congressional candidates who bet on their own races (platform action, no charges). Unidentified: the wallets that profited on the Feb 2026 Iran-strike contracts (Bubblemaps: six fresh wallets, about $1M) and other well-timed bets on Washington decisions; no trader has been named. Response: the White House warned staff in March 2026 that trading on non-public information breaks ethics rules, and spokesman David Ingle called implications that officials were betting 'baseless'.

sub_claims.statement: The prediction-market platforms have ties to the Trump family.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (re-verified from C25 and C38 sources; no new searches spent). Donald Trump Jr. became a strategic adviser to Kalshi in January 2025 and joined Polymarket's advisory board on 26 Aug 2025, the day 1789 Capital, where he is a partner, made an eight-figure strategic investment; in Aug 2026 a 1789 spokesperson confirmed plans to invest about $300M in a roughly $1B Polymarket round. Trump Media announced Truth Predict with Crypto.com in Oct 2025 and shelved it in Aug 2026. No filing or reporting documents any bet by a Trump family member on either platform. Responses: Don Jr.'s spokesperson says he does not engage with the federal government on behalf of companies he invests in or advises; Kalshi says he advises on marketing, not regulation.

sub_claims.statement: Any of these documented trades has been shown to rest on misuse of non-public information.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: absence of record through Nov 2026. Every trade above is a disclosed or reported trade; none has produced a charge, an inspector-general finding, an SEC or CFTC action, or an ethics-committee finding against the official, member of Congress or family member concerned. Several of the trades were mandated divestitures (Bondi, part of Duffy's) or made in accounts the filers say are managed by others (Trump, Duffy, Greene, Moskowitz, Khanna, Bresnahan). The only people charged in connection with government-decision bets are a soldier (Van Dyke) and, abroad, an Israeli reservist and civilian. Requests for investigation and their outcomes are the subject of C103.

corrections: Claimed: the Transportation Secretary sold stock shortly before the April 2025 tariff announcements. The record shows: Duffy's reported sales were on 11 and 13 February 2025, around the 13 February reciprocal-tariff plan, not in April.

Claimed (C58 summary, read broadly): no public evidence ties Trump to trades around the tariff pause. The record shows: that statement holds for the unidentified options traders, but one of Trump's own accounts made 327 purchases ($3.6M-$12.8M by range) on 8 April 2025, disclosed on 30 June 2026 (verified in the OGE report); the filing does not show who directed them. Applied to C58 on 2026-11-16.
C65 gives Bondi's sale as $1M-$5M of shares plus $250K-$500K of warrants (Bloomberg Law: $1M-$5.5M combined). The two ranges add to $1.25M-$5.5M; no change of substance.
Dates of Rep. Greene's purchases differ by outlet: most reports give 8-9 April 2025, others add 2 April or 3-4 April. The $21,021-$315,000 total is consistent.
C13 does not mention the reported unusual trading in ALT5 Sigma before the 11 Aug 2025 announcement; The Block reported it without accusing the company.
Unusual Machines' run-up (more than 220% in four weeks) came before Don Jr. joined on 27 Nov 2024, before the second term began.

2026-11-16 (audit): earlier text said Trump's 8 April 2025 purchases surfaced 'more than 14 months later' in 'July 2026'. The record shows: OGE received the annual report on 29 June 2026 and it was made public on 30 June, nearly 15 months after the trades and about 13 months after the 45-day 278-T deadline. The count (327, all purchases) and the $12.8M maximum were confirmed against Part 7; the minimum is about $3.6M.

2026-11-16 (audit): earlier text described an 'unnamed White House lawyer' and 'no response from Rana'. ProPublica names the lawyer (a career acting general counsel of the White House Office of Administration, who says his wife made the sale) and reports that Rana declined to comment; Rana was already ambassador to Slovakia when the report appeared.

2026-11-16 (audit): Gor's 27 March 2025 Trump Media sale ($15,001-$50,000) is now documented from his own 278-T; Scavino's 1 April sale remains single-source, and the reported Scavino capital gains are unverified.
2026-11-16 (audit): Van Dyke faces five counts, not only commodities-fraud and wire-fraud counts.
denials_and_context: A disclosed trade is not evidence of misuse of non-public information. Periodic transaction reports give only value ranges and dates, not time of day, profit, or who made the decision.

Bondi's ethics agreement required her to sell the Trump Media stake; DOJ did not answer early questions on the timing, and she later told a House hearing she complied with ethics rules and lost money (secondary summary).

The White House says Trump's assets are in fully discretionary accounts run by independent third-party institutions, that the advisers do not regularly communicate with him, and that there are no conflicts; it also pointed to trading by Nancy Pelosi. The Trump Organization says neither Trump nor his family selects, directs or approves investments or receives advance notice of trades. The accounts are not a blind trust, and the filing does not show who directed any trade.
The Transportation Department says an outside manager made Duffy's trades without his input and that some sales were required by his ethics agreement.
Greene says her portfolio manager 'bought the dip'; Moskowitz and Khanna say outside advisers or an independent trustee manage their trades; Bresnahan says he does not trade his own stocks.
Unusual Machines said only three senior officers, its board and counsel knew of Don Jr.'s planned role. ALT5 Sigma is not accused of wrongdoing in The Block's report.
Don Jr.'s spokesperson and Kalshi deny that he works on regulatory matters for the platforms; no bet by any Trump family member is documented.

Research limit: the first pass rested on search excerpts. In the audit, Trump's OGE annual report, Gor's 278-T, three ProPublica articles, Sludge, ABC News and Business Insider's Moskowitz report were read in full; USA Today (Scavino), CNN, Fortune and Bloomberg Law remain excerpts.

changes: Priority check: Part 7 of Trump's annual report (OGE received 29 June 2026; reviewer DJB, 30 June) was parsed line by line. 327 transactions dated 4/8/2025, all purchases, all in 'Investment Account #7'; range totals $3,629,327-$12,835,000. Confirmed. The reviewer's comments confirm a 45-day filing extension and late filing fees 'related to transactions not previously reported on 278-Ts'. Upgraded the source from reporting to the primary document read in full.

Added context from the same filing that cuts the other way: the account also made 462 trades on 4 April and 273 purchases on 10 April, and about 21,000 transactions in 2025; ABC News reads this as rebalancing.
Timing corrected: released 30 June 2026 (not 'July'); nearly 15 months after the trades and about 13 months after the 45-day deadline (not 'more than 14 months late').

White House response recorded exactly as reported, with the caveat that the 'fully discretionary accounts' wording is attributed to Anna Kelly without a confirmed occasion; added ABC's 'advisers who do not regularly communicate with Trump', Trump's own comment, and the Trump Organization statement.
Gor upgraded to documented from his own 278-T; Scavino kept single-source; the Scavino capital-gains report downgraded to unverified.

ProPublica articles read in full: Bondi ranges and no time of day confirmed; Duffy dates and amounts confirmed; Rana declined to comment (earlier text said no response found); the 'unnamed' White House lawyer is named by ProPublica with his response; USTR official added (no response).
Congress: Hern's trade dated 4 April; responses added for Khanna, Bresnahan and Greene; Hern's response not found; Bresnahan's count kept as single-source.
Verdict and confidence unchanged (mostly-accurate, medium): no charge or finding against any person named here was found through 16 Nov 2026.
